# GitHub Publish Changes

Use this skill when the user explicitly asks to publish local changes. The normal destination is the repository default branch. This workflow does not create a pull request by default.

## 目标分支与远端

1. Inspect `git status -sb`, the intended diff, and the configured remotes before staging. Preserve unrelated work.
2. Resolve the target remote from the user-authorized repository context. Do not silently replace a private or user-owned remote with an upstream source remote.
3. Resolve the default branch with two independent signals when both are available: `git ls-remote --symref <remote> HEAD` and the GitHub repository metadata field `defaultBranchRef`. If the signals disagree, stop and report the conflict. If only one signal is available, record which one was used. Never infer a branch from a familiar name.
4. Refuse to publish when the remote is not authorized, the repository identity is ambiguous, or the default-branch evidence is missing or conflicting.

## 默认发布

1. Confirm the exact file scope; stage explicit paths unless the user confirmed the whole worktree.
2. Run the narrowest relevant checks, commit the intended change, and publish to the resolved default branch with the resolved remote. Keep local and remote state aligned.
3. A pull request is not part of the default path. Create one only when the user explicitly requests it. Do not create a draft pull request implicitly.
4. Do not use force-push or overwrite a remote branch with an inferred name.

## 临时分支例外

Use a temporary branch only when the agent states the concrete reason (for example, an isolated review or a required safety boundary) and the user confirms. Once the first publishable commit exists, push that temporary branch so the local and remote refs remain consistent. After the user confirms the result, merge it into the resolved default branch using the normal non-forced flow, push the default branch, then delete the temporary branch locally and remotely and remove its temporary worktree. Retain it only when the user explicitly asks to keep it.

## 历史 patch-stack

Do not create, push, or retain patch-stack refs. Existing or historical patch-stack refs are report-only inventory; deleting them requires a separate explicit user approval and is never an implicit closeout action.

## 收尾

Report the resolved remote, the evidence used for the default branch, commit, checks, and final local/remote alignment. Stop on any mismatch instead of guessing.

# GitHub

Use this skill as the umbrella entrypoint for repository, pull request, and issue work. Resolve repository identity and local checkout context before taking an action.

## 路由

- Repository, issue, pull request, comment, label, or reaction triage stays connector-first.
- Review follow-up routes to `../gh-address-comments/SKILL.md`.
- CI debugging routes to `../gh-fix-ci/SKILL.md`.
- Publish changes routes immediately to `../yeet/SKILL.md`, whose normal destination is the repository default branch.

## 默认分支证据

When a publish request is routed, the publisher must resolve the target remote and default branch. It compares `git ls-remote --symref <remote> HEAD` with the GitHub metadata field `defaultBranchRef` when both are available; disagreement or missing authorization is a hard stop. A familiar branch name is never treated as evidence.

## 输出

State what was inspected, the selected specialist path, the authorized remote, and any remaining confirmation. Do not open a pull request as a side effect of ordinary triage or default publishing. Do not create, push, or retain patch-stack refs; historical refs are report-only unless the user separately approves deletion.
